user_input: Which mitigation options have direct, active mitigates relationships in Enterprise ATT&CK 17.1 to the technique mapped to Advanced Internet Protocol (IP) Scanner in AA23-165A? Start from LockBit affiliates and follow the three-hop actor-to-software-to-technique-to-mitigation path. Distinguish advisory observations from reference recommendations.
response:
LockBit affiliates' AnyDesk enables remote connections to network devices, which is mitigated by Network Intrusion Prevention (M1031). [E1, E2, E3, E4]
LockBit affiliates' Atera Remote Monitoring & Management (RMM) enables remote connections to network devices, which is mitigated by Network Intrusion Prevention (M1031). [E6, E2, E3, E4]
Network Service Discovery (T1046) is mitigated by Network Segmentation (M1030). [E8, E9]
LockBit affiliates' Backstab terminates antimalware-protected processes, which is mitigated by User Account Management (M1018). [E10, E11, E12]

reference: The AA23-165A Table 4 caption lists Advanced Internet Protocol (IP) Scanner as a tool used by LockBit affiliates. The selected advisory row maps its reported use to T1046 (Network Service Discovery). The direct, active mitigates relationships in Enterprise ATT&CK 17.1 connect this technique to: M1030 (Network Segmentation), M1031 (Network Intrusion Prevention), M1042 (Disable or Remove Feature or Program). These are reference mitigation associations, not incident-specific proof of effectiveness.
